title: Solve one- and two-step equations
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

sections.title: Undo adding or subtracting
sections.objective: Solve x + 5 = 12 and x − 3 = 8 by doing the opposite to both sides.
explain: An equation is a balance: whatever you do to one side, do to the other.
Check by putting your answer back in.

visual.caption: x + 3 balances 7. Take 3 from both sides.

sections.key: Do the opposite to both sides. Subtract to undo adding; add to undo subtracting.

worked.note: Undo it: subtract 5 from both sides.

sections.title: Undo multiplying or dividing
sections.objective: Solve 3x = 21 and x/4 = 6 by doing the opposite to both sides.
explain: 3x means 3 times x. x/4 means x divided by 4.
Signs follow the integer rules, and a fraction in front of x is undone by its reciprocal.
sections.key: Divide to undo multiplying; multiply to undo dividing. Do it to both sides.

worked.note: Undo it: divide both sides by 3.

sections.title: Two steps
sections.objective: Solve 3x + 5 = 20: undo the adding or subtracting first, then the multiplying or dividing.
explain: In 3x + 5, x was multiplied by 3 first, then 5 was added. Undo the last thing first, like taking off shoes before socks.
Dividing first is a common slip: the numbers stop working out.
sections.key: Undo in reverse order: first the adding or subtracting, then the multiplying or dividing.

worked.note: x was multiplied by 3, then 5 was added.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Solve one- and two-step equations with whole numbers, negatives and fractions.
explain: Now the problems are mixed: one step or two, whole numbers, negatives and fractions.
sections.key: Undo the last thing done to x first, doing the same to both sides. Then check.

worked.note: Undo the + 7: subtract 7 from both sides.
Undo the × (−2): divide both sides by −2.

hints.alg.equations.add-sub: What was done to x: adding or subtracting? Do the opposite to both sides.
hints.alg.equations.mult-div: x was multiplied or divided. Do the opposite to both sides: divide to undo multiplying, multiply to undo dividing.
hints.alg.equations.two-step: First undo the adding or subtracting, on both sides. Then undo the multiplying or dividing.
hints.alg.equations: Undo the last thing done to x first, doing the same to both sides. Then check your answer.

misconceptionMessages.alg.eq-add-same-op: To get x alone, undo what was done to it: if a number was added, subtract it from both sides.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eq-add-sign: The size is right, but check the sign. Put your answer back into the equation to check.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eq-mult-same-op: To undo multiplying, divide (and to undo dividing, multiply). Do the opposite of what was done to x.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eq-mult-wrong-inverse: 3x means 3 times x, so undo it by dividing by 3, not subtracting 3.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eq-flipped-division: Divide the other side by the number in front of x: in 6x = 4, x = 4 ÷ 6, not 6 ÷ 4.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eq-mult-sign: Check the sign with the integer rules: dividing by a negative changes the sign.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eq-stopped-early: You undid the adding or subtracting. Now there's still a number multiplying x: undo that too.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eq-two-wrong-inverse: To undo adding a number, subtract it from both sides (and to undo subtracting, add).
misconceptionMessages.alg.eq-divide-first: Undo the adding or subtracting first, then the multiplying. Dividing first only works if you divide every part of both sides.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eq-two-sign: Both steps are right, but check the sign. Put your answer back into the equation to check.
